$comment: Measured tuning profile. Every value below was measured on an idle NVIDIA GB10 and carries its provenance. Nothing here is extrapolated or guessed. Re-generate with: pulse tune

hardware.name: NVIDIA GB10
hardware.provenance: bench_gb10_streaming on an idle GPU; peak is the vendor figure

model.provenance: 6.70 GB / 184.6 GB/s. Confirmed: no-drafter batch-1 decode measures 27.54 tok/s = 36.3 ms/token

launch_flags.ubatch_provenance: ubatch 1024 measured worse than 512 on prefill (389 vs 656 tok/s). Do not raise.
launch_flags.batch_provenance: prompts above 2048 tokens fail with the default batch size

parallel_slots.provenance: true batched decode scales 27.54 -> 133.08 tok/s from B=1 to B=16 (llama-batched-bench). llama-server defaults to n_slots=4, which saturates at 73.08 tok/s aggregate with 16 clients; 16 slots reaches 117.71.

v1.note: K=4 (= block_size) beats K=3 on throughput: 63.77 vs 58.08 tok/s. K=3 gives higher acceptance (78.29% vs 72.28%) but fewer tokens per step. Use the full block.

drafters.recommended_provenance: v1 at K=4 is the measured best single-stream config on realistic code context

k_policy.rule: never request K above the drafter's block_size
k_policy.provenance: K=5 and K=7 are byte-identical to K=4 with the v1 drafter (4.03 tok/step, 77.52% acceptance, 62.5 ms/step). --spec-draft-n-max past block_size is a no-op.

speculation_by_load.rule: speculate at low concurrency, disable at high concurrency
speculation_by_load.provenance: bench/conc.py against a 16-slot server, 128 tokens per request, temperature 0
speculation_by_load.caveat: llama-server cannot toggle speculation per request: the schema fields speculative.n_max / n_min are compiled out behind '#if 0' in tools/server/server-schema.cpp, and the decode path reads params_base.speculative. Acting on this policy currently requires two backends.

known_negative_results.cuda_graphs: GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON measured 61.84 vs 62.40 tok/s - no effect. Graphs are disabled at runtime because Gated DeltaNet nodes fail ggml_cuda_graph_check_compability.
known_negative_results.ptq1_0_target: smaller target measured 22% slower (51.73 vs 65.96 tok/s)
known_negative_results.ngram_stacking: counters byte-identical to the drafter alone; never engaged
known_negative_results.batched_lm_head_kernel: no gain available. mul_mat_vec_q already amortises the weight read across ncols_dst; measured +10% kernel time for 2.5x the columns.

vs_stock_defaults.$comment: Measured today, idle GB10, same model, same harness (bench/conc.py), 128 tokens/request, temp 0.
vs_stock_defaults.tuned: pulse serve  (16 slots, -fa on, -ub 512, drafter by load policy)

design_curve.$comment: Throughput vs accepted-tokens-per-step at 100% acceptance, measured with a model-free n-gram drafter on repetitive text. This is the hardware ceiling for any drafter, and the spec any drafter must be designed against.
design_curve.method: llama-speculative-simple --spec-type ngram-simple --spec-ngram-simple-size-m M, idle GB10, temp 0
design_curve.base_is_the_weight_sweep: 36.65 ms measured vs 36.3 ms predicted from 6.70 GB / 184.6 GB/s
design_curve.discontinuity_at_8: ncols_dst crosses MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 and dispatch falls from mul_mat_vec_q to MMQ: +14.5 ms for +1.9 tokens. MMQ base ~65 ms, marginal ~1.0 ms/row.
design_curve.threshold_is_correctly_tuned_below_8: forcing MMQ earlier via GGML_MMVQ_MAX measured 34% worse (100.78 -> 75.21 tok/s at 5 rows). Raising it above 8 asserts: mmvq is only template-instantiated to ncols_dst=8, so rows 9-15 are forced onto MMQ although the measured crossover is ~15.

remaining_levers.$comment: Both quantified against the measured design curve. Together they clear 100 tok/s single-stream.

lever_1_drafter_path_overhead.evidence: at 3.86 tok/step the n-gram curve gives 44.9 ms/step; the dspark drafter measures 60.6 ms. Of the 15.7 ms gap only 3.27 ms is the drafter's own 603 MB sweep.

lever_2_deeper_block.evidence: v1 already reaches 90.18% acceptance at depth 3 and 72-78% at depth 3-4

remaining_levers.both: ~100+ tok/s single-stream, no change to the target model
